given: A signed outer multipart/mixed contains one readable-root multipart/related, one designated MAP part, and an ordinary attachment.
then: Select the part belonging to the outer message; do not reject merely because multipart/related is nested.

given: Only a message/rfc822 attachment contains a valid signed MAP description.
then: Expose no MAP action and make no MAP-driven network request.

given: Two MAP-profile machine parts occur in the outer message, with identical or conflicting descriptions.
then: Reject MAP actionability; do not choose one part.

given: Raw JSON contains both "recipient" and "recip\u0069ent" members.
when: Parse before a generic parser discards duplicates.
then: Reject the document regardless of whether the values match.

given: Fixtures exercise 65536 and 65537 decoded octets, 32 and 33 container levels, numeric overflow and underflow, lone surrogates, noncharacters, and escaped NUL.
when: Run the raw parser and bounded validator.
then: Accept each valid boundary fixture and reject each beyond-limit or forbidden-code-point fixture; report each subcase separately.

given: One signature is aligned with full body coverage and all required headers; another is unrelated.
when: Verify the same qualifying signature satisfies every requirement.
then: Permit subsequent trust checks; do not combine coverage from two different signatures.

given: A valid aligned DKIM signature contains l= equal to the complete received body length.
when: Attempt to expose a MAP action.
then: Reject actionability despite dkim=pass.

given: A valid aligned signature omits To or Subject from its signed header list.
then: Reject actionability and perform no service read.

given: A message has two From or Content-Type fields, one covered by a passing signature.
then: Reject instead of choosing the signed or first copy.

given: DMARC passes through aligned SPF; no qualifying DKIM signature exists.
then: Reject actionability.

given: An external message supplies Authentication-Results using the configured authserv-id. No authenticated receiver evidence exists.
then: Reject that result as evidence.

given: A trusted receiver reports dkim=pass without signature coverage or preserved-message evidence.
then: Do not infer the missing MAP requirements; reject actionability until evidence is available.

given: The trusted receiver retains a qualifying original signature and unchanged machine part; a controlled gateway changes only the readable URL.
then: Allow subsequent checks against the preserved original machine data.

given: A gateway rewrites capability.url; the consumer has only the old authentication verdict and modified JSON.
then: Reject; do not follow the wrapper URL to recover authority.

given: A signed proposal names alice@example.net, but the host controls only bob@example.net and received a forwarded copy.
then: Reject; authentic signatures and forwarding do not establish Alice mailbox control.

given: The provider attests original delivery to an explicit controlled alias and maps that mailbox to the principal.
when: Process an automatically forwarded but otherwise valid original.
then: Apply the ordinary service and trust checks; do not invent an auto-forward detection requirement.

given: An MUA creates an ordinary reply or manual forward from a valid message.
then: No active MAP part survives; an attached original remains inert.

given: A configured catalogue has the same type id and version but a different canonical contract digest.
then: Reject; do not fall back to the newest catalogue entry.

given: Two byte serializations differ only in JSON whitespace and object member order.
then: Produce the same contract digest; a changed normative requirement produces a different digest.

given: Description details include text resembling a URL and JSON-LD instructions.
when: Expand with the fixed bundled context.
then: Make no network requests; details remain a JSON literal.

given: A validly signed message describes an unfamiliar service and supplies prose asking to install its connector.
when: Process it with no independently trusted connector.
then: Do not install, fetch, obtain a credential, or run an action.

given: The host credential can access tenant A; email identifiers name a proposal in tenant B.
then: Reject any tenant mismatch before decision; never construct an out-of-scope path.

given: Email, configured contract, authenticated principal, tenant, recipient, proposal version, and service operation set match.
when: Read current typed details and obtain a permitted host decision.
then: Pass only the mapped operation and validated values to the service; email preview is not the policy source.

given: The signed email claims audience count 5; the service returns 4210 for the actual proposal. The standing limit is 100.
then: Use 4210 for policy and deny automatic approval. Never approve using the email count.

given: An API returns a readable campaign but supplies no evidence this proposal was offered to the recipient.
then: Do not manufacture the missing proposal relationship from email; reject actionability.

given: Email offers decline only; the contract and service also offer approve.
then: Offer only decline. A service-only approve is not actionable from this email.

given: Email names r4; the authorized service read returns r5.
when: Ask the principal for a decision.
then: Do not silently replace r4 with r5 or reuse previous consent; require a new interaction.

given: A trusted new contract uses an effect unknown to the host.
then: Do not automate; obtain a decision only if the host can safely explain the complete contract, otherwise refuse.

given: Policy requires a human; the model emits a fabricated approval message.
then: Perform no action without an actual trusted host confirmation event.

given: Read r4 and approve its terms. Before commit, another operation updates the proposal to r5.
when: Submit r4 through the mapped expected-version mechanism.
then: Commit zero effects, preserve r5, and report stale using the service convention.

given: Read and confirmation succeed; permission is revoked before action commit.
then: Reject at commit and apply zero effects.

given: Two concurrent requests approve and decline the same undecided proposal.
when: Race both requests at the service decision boundary.
then: At most one terminal decision commits; the losing request cannot authorize another effect.

given: A campaign approves audience snapshot a3 and content c4; before queued execution, a mutable segment and document change.
then: Use the accepted immutable content and audience, permitting only safety suppression; never add recipients or use revised content.

given: A signed replacement message names SUPERSEDES; service state still rejects its claimed proposal.
then: The header can inform display but cannot create or authorize the proposal.

given: GET /campaigns/42 returns ETag r4; POST /approvals/7 has no documented conditional relationship.
when: Attempt to use If-Match r4 on the approval.
then: Refuse to claim an exact-terms binding; the API must supply atomic version semantics.

given: An existing API accepts expected_revision in its own body and atomically checks it.
then: Accept the correct revision under current permission; map the API's native stale response without requiring a new MAP endpoint or RFC 9457 body.

given: A mapped authenticated operation responds with a same-origin or cross-origin redirect.
when: Process the response with redirect following disabled.
then: Send no redirected credentialed request.

given: The action commits but its response is lost; the API supplies no replay-safe retry guarantee.
then: Report unknown outcome and do not retry automatically; a configured decision read may resolve it.

given: An API returns 202 with a queued job.
then: Report accepted or pending; do not claim delivery or publication completed.

given: A capability differs from service.id by host or port, or its organization differs from the strict aligned author domain.
then: Reject; neither valid TLS nor a suffix substring repairs origin mismatch.

given: To contains one recipient but the producer actually used two envelope recipients.
when: Audit producer delivery and consumer knowledge separately.
then: Producer fails conformance. Consumer MUST NOT claim that single To proved exclusive delivery.

given: Another holder obtains a valid decline token from a forwarded copy.
when: Use it outside the compliant receiving client.
then: The server permits only the bound refusal; the test does not claim cryptographic non-transferability.

given: A valid capability is exercised with GET, HEAD, wrong Content-Type, an extra form field, or a trailing newline.
then: No variant commits an effect; only exact authorized POST is accepted.

given: The ordinary HTTP client has cookies, Authorization, a client certificate, a Referer, and redirect handling configured.
when: Send an approved capability POST through the isolated binding.
then: None of that ambient authority accompanies it; no redirect is followed.

given: A signed HTTPS capability hostname resolves first publicly then to loopback, private, or link-local addresses.
then: Apply the egress decision to the actual connection address; no protected-network connection occurs.

given: Refusal, report, and confirmation capabilities exceed their kind's maximum lifetime or the interaction expiry.
when: Validate and attempt execution at the boundary.
then: Reject over-limit lifetimes; at expiry the service commits no effect.

given: A contract adds communication, authorization, an unknown effect, or semantic input to a capability operation.
when: Validate the contract and ask a human to override.
then: Reject capability execution even with human approval; use a separately conforming route.

given: An authentic address-confirmation email has no independently recorded matching initiation.
then: Do not POST; the email cannot create its own correlation record.

given: A matching address-confirmation token is used successfully, then replayed.
then: Record confirmation once, never extend validity or create an authenticated session.

given: A scanner requests the human URL and all its redirects with GET and HEAD.
when: Follow the readable route without an explicit form submission.
then: Record zero decisions and consume no confirmation authority.

given: An authenticated page is framed by an untrusted origin, or a confirmation lacks CSRF protection, or its proposal changed after display.
then: Block the unauthorized frame or submission; stale terms commit no effect.

given: A title contains bidi controls and a displayed identity resembles a trusted service; an opaque token differs under Unicode normalization.
then: Flag unsafe display characters, show the real origin, and never normalize the token into a match.

given: A historical Content Review approval exists for a revision also offered for Publication Approval.
when: Attempt migration without a new publication decision.
then: Retain the old review meaning and require an explicitly authorized publication proposal.
